# Khandhakapucchāvāra (Pvr 6)

**ID:** Pvr 6
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Khandhakapucchāvāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khandhakapucchāvāra* (also known as the *Khandhakapucchā*) is the sixth treatise of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [Horner 1966]. The text comprises a catechism that poses questions on the contents and legal issues of each chapter of the Khandhakas, surveying the ten chapters of the *Mahāvagga* and the twelve of the *Cullavagga* [Horner 1966]. While framed around queries regarding the number of offences occurring across these chapters, I.B. Horner observes, following the commentary, that it inquires into the categories and classes of offences rather than raw numerical counts [Horner 1966]. The text begins with a question and answer regarding ordination (*upasampadā*) with its provenance and demonstration, determining the relevant offences according to eminent sentences [Horner 1966].

 Complete English translations have been published by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner 1966].

**Sources**

- [Horner 1966] I.B. Horner, The Book of the Discipline (Vinaya-Piṭaka), Vol. VI: Parivāra (London: Pali Text Society, 1966) — Provided analysis of the alternative title, structure, coverage of the Mahāvagga and Cullavagga, commentary use, and translated opening formula.
